case_name: State of Haryana v Balkar Singh and Others

statutes.act: And 323 Read With Section 34 Of The Indian Penal Code

facts: On 9.2.1993 at about 8.00 A. M. ,Dev Singh was heading from the house to his fields carrying a Sutli and Sua for the purpose of stitching the bags in which potatoes were to be packed and he had hardly covered a distance of 4/5 yards when he found accused Balkar Singh, Chuhar Singh, Surinder Singh, Sher Singh (hereinafter referred to as 'deceased') and injured Shamsher Singh standing near the tubewell of Chuhar Singh...
Thereafter there was free exchange of danda blows from both sides. Shamsher Singh was injured by all the three accused, who received injuries on both shoulders, left side of the chest and head.

Injured Sher Singh and Shamsher Singh were got medico-legally examined. Sher Singh, who had been referred to P.G.I. Chandigarh, succumbed to the injuries on 13.2.1993, where upon Faqir Chand ASI (PW-12) conducted inquest proceedings Ex. PJ/3 and autopsy was conducted by Dr. B.Suri (PW-14).
The occurrence took place in the course of free fight and there were more severe injuries caused on the person of the accused person than the deceased and the so called eye witness.
petitioner_arguments: Analysis made by the trial court and the High Court and the conclusions arrived at are not in line with the evidence adduced including that of the eye-witness and injured eye- witness.
respondent_arguments: The judgment of the trial court as upheld by the High Court is supported.
court_reasoning: There is no scope for interference in this appeal which is accordingly dismissed.
The view taken by the trial court was a possible view and the High Court did not interfere.
The occurrence took place in the course of free fight and there were more severe injuries caused on the person of the accused person than the deceased and the so called eye witness.
cases_cited: State of Haryana v Balkar Singh
